question: During a multi region switchover, what is causing some customers to get bursty too many requests and occasional service unavailable responses because different parts of the traffic gatekeeper disagree briefly on the time boundary used for quota calculations?
answer: A race between epoch (quota time-boundary) transitions and the async, non-atomically versioned policy cache refresh causes proxy, orchestrator, and host rate controllers to use inconsistent epoch anchors during failover/restarts. That brief mismatch makes the burst evaluator miscompute credits (treating old/missing anchors as no-burst), leading to overly aggressive admission drops and resulting 429 spikes and some downstream 503s.
